name: Sermilik
body:
SERMILIK
CR 7

The patches of ice in the water burst forth as a white, bear-like creature coated in ice and hunger in its eyes.

XP 3,200
N Large magical beast (cold)
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +9
Aura cold aura (10 ft., DC 20)

DEFENSE

AC 25, touch 13, flat-footed 21 (+4 Dex, +12 natural, –1 size)
hp 75 (6d10+42)
Fort +11, Ref +8, Will +4
Immune cold; Weakness fire

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., swim 30 ft.
Melee bite +13 (1d8+8), 2 claws +13 (1d6+8 plus grab)
Space 50 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks breath weapon (30-ft. cone, 6d6 cold damage, Reflex DC 20 half, usable every 1d4 rounds)

STATISTICS

Str 26, Dex 18, Con 24, Int 2, Wis 16, Cha 10
Base Atk +6; CMB +15 (+19 grapple); CMD 28 (32 vs. trip)
Feats Endurance, Run, Skill Focus (Survival)
Skills Perception +9, Survival +8, Swim +20
Languages Abyssal, Common, Draconic, Dwarven, Giant, Orc
SQ hold breath, icy armor

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Cold Aura (Su)

A sermilik constantly outputs an aura of frigid air.

Any creature entering or beginning their turn within the aura must make a Fortitude save or take 1d6 cold damage. This is a cold effect and the DC is Constitution-based.

Hold Breath (Ex)

A sermilik can hold its breath for a number of minutes equal to 6 times its Constitution score before it risks drowning.

Icy Armor (Su)

A sermilik is coated in a thick hide of ice that grants them a +4 enhancement bonus to natural armor. However, if they take 20 or more fire damage, the AC bonus is lost until they can submerge themselves in water for 1 full round. At which point, their cold aura reforms this armor.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold coastlines or plains
Organization solitary or pair
Treasure none

This ice-clad ursine lives along the coastlines of the polar seas. Each resembles a stocky polar bear, but its white coat is covered in layers of icicles and overlapping frozen chunks of ice. They are ambush predators that hide under the surface of the water, with their frozen back and looking like nothing more than a jagged ice floe before they burst forth to savage their prey.
